newsitem.title: USA: USDA puts 97/98 cotton crop at 18.5 million bales.
newsitem.headline: USDA puts 97/98 cotton crop at 18.5 million bales.

text.p: The Agriculture Department estimated on Tuesday 1997/98 U.S. cotton production at 18.5 million bales, 2.4 percent below 1996/97 levels.
Speaking at the USDA's annual Agricultural Outlook Forum, a USDA analyst said 18.0 million bales would be upland cotton production.

Planted cotton acreage in 1997/98 was projected at 14.0 million acres, down 4.6 percent from last year. Analysts said some cotton would shift to corn and soybean acres due to currently good prices for those crops.
U.S. cotton exports in 1997/98 were projected at 7.0 million bales, up 7.7 percent from the previous year's level.

USDA said that coupled with the current beginning stock estimate of 4.45 million bales, total U.S. cotton supplies next season would reach 23 million bales, one million above 96/97 supplies, and the second-highest U.S. cotton supply level in the last 30 years.
